ust.method: Overnight = New York closes strictly before each Jakarta close (New York shuts at about 04:00–05:00 Jakarta). Hedged = INDOGB 10Y minus β × US 10Y, β the trailing 26-week weekly beta known at the time. All variants walk-forward, z-scores vs trailing 52 weeks, thresholds ±0.5, hit rates over the next 4 weeks. The 'Beta 3Y' slot carries the INDOGB 15Y.

notes.headline: Asia's tech rout skipped Jakarta: JCI +0.4% with Rp328bn of foreign buying and a flat rupiah, but the 10Y INDOGB holds 7.70%, 47bp higher in four weeks and almost all of it local. Signal −0.64: bond sell-off
notes.now: Foreign money is still out of Indonesian stocks over the month, but Friday showed some resilience. A US tech sell-off took the Kospi down 8% at the open; the JCI fell 2% in the morning yet closed 0.4% higher at 5,050 as foreigners bought a net Rp328bn, mostly big banks ahead of MSCI's Nov 11 review. It is still 17% down in four weeks, and the rupiah, flat at 18,089 (JISDOR 18,130), is 1.7% weaker over the same span even as FX reserves rose $0.5bn to $146.8bn. Bonds have paid through price: the 10Y INDOGB is up 47bp in four weeks to 7.70%, though local buyers pushed the 2–4Y sector 6–8bp lower today. Three of the four signal parts still point to a sell-off (JCI 4-week z −1.78, rupiah z +0.76, 10Y trend z +1.63), and only the spread part is bond-bullish: INDOGBs pay 286bp over Treasuries, 45bp above their 26-week average (z +1.59) and a new 52-week high; the signal is −0.64, up from −0.76 four weeks ago. Treasuries explain almost none of the trend: the US 10Y fell 38bp in four weeks and the weekly beta is −0.11, so the move splits into +4bp 'global' and +43bp local. On the day the link broke: Thursday's 5.5bp New York rally implied about −1.6bp for INDOGBs at the 1-year daily beta of 0.29, yet the 10Y moved −0.1bp; INDOGBs follow 10bp-plus US moves in the same direction 68–80% of the time, but smaller ones much less reliably. The signal has read sell-off since Oct 2 and the 10Y is 54bp higher since, a clear hit for this episode. Its full record is modest (Sharpe 0.36 since June 2022, sell-off calls right 54%), but since September 2024, when foreign flows took over, it scores 1.11 outright and 1.38 hedged. Our read for the next 2–4 weeks: stay underweight duration until BI acts or the rupiah holds below 18,100 for a week; a second day of foreign equity buying is encouraging, and with the spread cushion at its widest of the year the turn, when it comes, should be fast.
notes.flip: The signal returns to neutral above −0.5: roughly, the JCI 4-week return back above −5% or the 10Y's 4-week rise slowing below 20bp, with USD/IDR flat or lower. A move to bond rally (above +0.5) needs a JCI rebound and a firmer rupiah together, the pattern that started the April 2025 rally. The policy triggers are a BI-Rate hike that steadies the rupiah (bearish for the front end on the day, bullish for the trend after) or MSCI softening its Standalone proposal.
phases: JCI 6,500–7,250 while the 10Y rose from 6.2% to a 7.58% peak in October 2022 as global rates surged; stocks held up on the commodity boom.
JCI 6,630–7,380 and 10Y 6.19–7.21%. Stocks and bonds drifted without a clear link, and the signal's calls lost money (Sharpe −0.3 from 2022 to August 2024).
JCI fell from 7,812 to 6,258 while the 10Y rose from 6.43% to 7.19%: stocks, rupiah and bonds sold off together, the pattern the signal is built for. Its record improves sharply from here.
JCI climbed from 6,262 to a record 9,075 on Jan 15, 2026, and the 10Y fell to 5.93% in October 2025 as foreign money returned and BI eased.

MSCI froze Indonesian index changes in January and on Oct 15 proposed Standalone status; BI hiked 100bp to 5.75% by June and now weighs more, while a wiretapping case against senior police officers adds political risk. JCI −44% to about 5,050, 10Y up 159bp to 7.70%: the second and deeper foreign exit, though foreigners still bought SBN in October.
notes.caveats: These are proxies, not reported fund flows: daily foreign SBN holdings (DJPPR) and equity flows (IDX) are not machine-readable for the dashboard, so the rupiah and the JCI stand in for foreign money. Before Oct 29, 2026 the 10Y is CNBC's benchmark-bond yield rather than PHEI's IGSYC, with repeated stale prints removed. The back-test runs from June 2022 (228 weeks): the live signal makes 89bp outright (Sharpe 0.36) against −71bp for always holding the 10Y; rally calls were right 49% of the time and sell-off calls 54%. Variants that use the US 10Y trend score higher over the whole sample (Sharpe up to 0.80) but were picked after the fact and are not live. Weekly data, 4-week horizon; not a trading system.
